records.source: מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ףלָמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים זָנַ֣חְתָּ לָנֶ֑צַח יֶעְשַׁ֥ן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ בְּצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: A maskil of Asaph. Why, God, have you rejected forever? [Why] does your anger smoke against [the] sheep of your pasture?
pieces: A maskil of Asaph. \q God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cast us off for good? \q Why does {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger burn and smoke against the flock {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tend?

L.1: A maskil of Asaph. \q Why, God, have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rejected [us] forever? \q [Why] does {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger smoke against the sheep of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} pasture?

R.1: A song of Asaph, to teach and give insight. \q God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turned away from us for so long? \q Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} so angry with us, the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} care for like sheep?

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: maskil: a song of insight, or a skillful song
decisions.reason: As in 42:1: the word comes from the verb "to have insight, act wisely"; its exact sense as a heading is no longer known.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work. Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: a lament for the burned temple
decisions.reason: The psalm mourns the destruction of the sanctuary and the meeting places of God (verses 3-8). This fits the burning of the temple by the Babylonians in 587 BC (2 Kings 25:9; Lamentations 2:7). Psalm 79 is a lament over the same disaster.

decisions.choice: your anger smokes: your anger burns
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as fire and smoke rising from the nostrils (18:9).

decisions.choice: the sheep of your pasture: God's people
decisions.reason: Israel is the flock that God shepherds (79:13; 95:7; 100:3).

decisions.choice: A song of Asaph, to teach and give insight
decisions.reason: As in 42:1, Readable gives the likely sense of maskil (m2).

records.heading: Remember your people and your ruined sanctuary

records.source: זְכֹ֤ר עֲדָתְךָ֨׀קָ֘נִ֤יתָ קֶּ֗דֶם גָּ֭אַלְתָּ שֵׁ֣בֶט נַחֲלָתֶ֑ךָ הַר־צִ֝יּ֗וֹן זֶ֤ה׀שָׁכַ֬נְתָּ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Remember your congregation [which] you acquired of old, [which] you redeemed [as the] tribe of your inheritance, Mount Zion, this [where] you have dwelt in it.
pieces: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own long ago, \q the tribe {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bought back to be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance; \q remember Mount Zion, where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} home.

L.2: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} congregation, [which] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} acquired of old, \q [which] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed [as the] tribe of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, \q Mount Zion, where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have dwelt.

R.2: Remember the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} chose long ago to be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own. \q You set them free to be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} special tribe. \q Remember Mount Zion, where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have lived.

decisions.choice: Exodus 15:13-17
decisions.reason: The words echo the song at the sea: the people God "redeemed" and "acquired", brought to "the mountain of your inheritance" where he would dwell (Exodus 15:13, 16-17).

decisions.choice: acquired: made your own
decisions.reason: The verb (qanah) means to get or buy, and sometimes to make (Deuteronomy 32:6).

decisions.choice: your inheritance: your own possession
decisions.reason: Israel is the people God claimed as his own share (28:9; 33:12).

decisions.choice: remember
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "remember" so that Mount Zion is clearly the second thing God is asked to remember.

records.source: הָרִ֣ימָה פְ֭עָמֶיךָ לְמַשֻּׁא֣וֹת נֶ֑צַח כָּל־הֵרַ֖ע אוֹיֵ֣ב בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: Lift up your steps to [the] perpetual ruins; everything [the] enemy has damaged in the sanctuary.
pieces: Come, make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way over these ruins that never end; \q the enemy has smashed everything in the holy place.

L.3: Lift up {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} steps to the everlasting ruins; \q the enemy has damaged everything in the sanctuary.

R.3: Come and look at what is left of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple. It lies in ruins that seem to go on forever. \q The enemy has destroyed everything in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy place.

decisions.choice: lift up your steps: come quickly, come and see
decisions.reason: God is asked to hurry over to see the ruins for himself.

decisions.choice: perpetual ruins: ruins that seem endless
decisions.reason: The ruins (mashshu'ot, as in 73:18) look as if they will last forever; "perpetual" (netsach) is the word of verse 1, "forever".

decisions.choice: what is left of your temple
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the ruins are those of the temple (verses 3-7).

records.source: שָׁאֲג֣וּ צֹ֭רְרֶיךָ בְּקֶ֣רֶב מוֹעֲדֶ֑ךָ שָׂ֖מוּ אוֹתֹתָ֣ם אֹתֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Your foes roared in [the] midst of your meeting place; they set up their signs [as] signs.
pieces: Your enemies roared in the middle of the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} met with us; \q they set up their own banners as signs.

L.4: Your foes have roared in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} meeting place; \q they have set up their signs [as] signs.

R.4: Your enemies shouted in the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} met with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. \q They put up their flags to show they had won.

decisions.choice: your meeting place: the temple
decisions.reason: The word (mo'ed) is the place or time of meeting; the tent of meeting was where God met with Israel (Exodus 33:7).

decisions.choice: their signs: military standards, or the enemy's religious symbols
decisions.reason: The enemies set up their own "signs" in the temple, perhaps army standards, perhaps the symbols of their gods. Verse 9 sets against this that Israel sees no signs from God.

records.source: יִ֭וָּדַע כְּמֵבִ֣יא לְמָ֑עְלָה בִּֽסֲבָךְ־עֵ֝֗ץ קַרְדֻּמּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: It was known like [one] bringing up in a thicket of trees axes.
pieces: They seemed like woodcutters lifting their axes \q against a dense stand of trees.

L.5: It was known like [one who] brings up axes \q into a thicket of trees.

R.5: They were like people chopping down trees \q in a forest with axes.

decisions.choice: it was known like one bringing up axes: the enemy hacked like woodcutters
alternatives: it looked like someone raising axes
decisions.reason: The words are very hard. The general sense is clear: the enemy hacked at the temple's woodwork (verse 6) as woodcutters hack at a thicket.

decisions.choice: They seemed like (B); They were like (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense of "it was known" (m1).

records.source: וְ֭עַתָּה פִּתּוּחֶ֣יהָ יָּ֑חַד בְּכַשִּׁ֥יל וְ֝כֵֽילַפֹּ֗ת יַהֲלֹמֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And now its carvings altogether with hatchet and hammers they strike down.
pieces: And now they hack away at all its carved panels \q with hatchets and hammers.

L.6: And now its carvings, all of them, \q they strike down with hatchet and hammers.

R.6: They used axes and hammers \q to smash all the carved wood inside.

decisions.choice: and now: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The words are written as "and the time" and marked to be read as "and now". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: its carvings: the carved wood of the temple
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple was lined with cedar carved with flowers, palms and cherubim (1 Kings 6:18, 29).

decisions.choice: hatchet and hammers: tools for breaking
decisions.reason: Both words are rare; they name tools for cutting and smashing.

records.source: שִׁלְח֣וּ בָ֭אֵשׁ מִקְדָּשֶׁ֑ךָ לָ֝אָ֗רֶץ חִלְּל֥וּ מִֽשְׁכַּן־שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: They sent into the fire your sanctuary; to the ground they profaned [the] dwelling of your name.
pieces: They set {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary on fire; \q they dragged the home of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name down to the ground and defiled it.

L.7: They have sent {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuary into the fire; \q to the ground they have profaned the dwelling place of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.7: They burned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple. \q They tore down the house that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and made it unclean.

decisions.choice: profaned to the ground: defiled by throwing it down
decisions.reason: They treated the holy place as common, and brought it down to the ground (89:40).

decisions.choice: the dwelling of your name: the place where God's presence was known
decisions.reason: God chose a place "to make his name dwell there" (Deuteronomy 12:11): the temple was where his presence was known and called on.

decisions.choice: the house that belongs to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m2).

records.source: אָמְר֣וּ בְ֭לִבָּם נִינָ֣ם יָ֑חַד שָׂרְפ֖וּ כָל־מוֹעֲדֵי־אֵ֣ל בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: They said in their heart, Let us oppress them altogether; they burned all [the] meeting places of God in the land.
pieces: In their hearts they said, "Let us beat them down, all of them!" \q They set fire to all God's meeting places throughout the land.

L.8: They said in their heart, "Let us crush them all together." \q They burned all the meeting places of God in the land.

R.8: They thought, "We will wipe them all out!" \q They burned down every place in the land where people met to worship God.

decisions.choice: the meeting places of God: places where people met to worship
decisions.reason: The same word (mo'ed) as "meeting place" in verse 4, here plural: places across the land where God was worshiped. What they were is not known.

decisions.choice: said in their heart: thought to themselves
decisions.reason: As in 10:6 and 14:1.

records.source: אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֥א רָ֫אִ֥ינוּ אֵֽין־ע֥וֹד נָבִ֑יא וְלֹֽא־אִ֝תָּ֗נוּ יֹדֵ֥עַ עַד־מָֽה׃
records.gloss: Our signs we have not seen; there is no longer a prophet, and there is not with us [one who] knows until when.
pieces: We see no signs for us anymore; \q no prophet is left, \q and no one among us can say how long it will be.

L.9: Our signs we have not seen; \q there is no longer a prophet, \q and there is no [one] with us who knows how long.

R.9: We see no miracles from God. \q There are no more prophets. \q No one here can tell us how long this will go on.

decisions.choice: our signs: signs from God for us
decisions.reason: Against the enemy's signs in the temple (verse 4), Israel sees no sign that God is with them: no wonders, no word.

decisions.choice: no prophet: no word from God
decisions.reason: Without a prophet no one can say how long the disaster will last (Lamentations 2:9; Amos 8:11).

decisions.choice: miracles from God
decisions.reason: Readable says whose signs are meant (m1).

records.source: עַד־מָתַ֣י אֱ֭לֹהִים יְחָ֣רֶף צָ֑ר יְנָ֘אֵ֤ץ אוֹיֵ֖ב שִׁמְךָ֣ לָנֶֽצַח׃
records.gloss: Until when, God, will [the] foe taunt? Will [the] enemy spurn your name forever?
pieces: How long, God, will the enemy jeer? \q Will the foe go on insulting {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever?

L.10: How long, God, will [the] foe taunt? \q Will [the] enemy spurn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever?

R.10: God, how long will the enemy make fun of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q Will they keep insulting {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever?

decisions.choice: taunt, spurn: insult and treat with contempt
decisions.reason: The enemy's mockery is aimed at God himself, at his name (verse 18).

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself; Readable says "you".

records.source: לָ֤מָּה תָשִׁ֣יב יָ֭דְךָ וִֽימִינֶ֑ךָ מִקֶּ֖רֶב חֵֽיקְךָ֣ כַלֵּֽה׃
records.gloss: Why do you draw back your hand, and your right hand? From [the] midst of your bosom, destroy!
pieces: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand still, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong right hand? \q Pull it out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cloak and make an end of them!

L.11: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} draw back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, even {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand? \q From the midst of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} bosom, destroy [them]!

R.11: Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do nothing? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} powerful hand hidden away? \q Use it and destroy them!

decisions.choice: your bosom: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The word is written with letters that could read "your statute" and is marked to be read as "your bosom", which fits the picture. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: from the midst of your bosom: take your hand out of the fold of your robe
decisions.reason: God is pictured with his hand tucked into the fold of his garment, doing nothing (Exodus 4:6-7). He is asked to draw it out and strike.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: "Destroy" has no object; the enemies are meant.

records.source: וֵ֭אלֹהִים מַלְכִּ֣י מִקֶּ֑דֶם פֹּעֵ֥ל יְ֝שׁוּע֗וֹת בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And God [is] my King from of old, working salvation in [the] midst of the earth.
pieces: But God has been my King since ancient times, \q bringing rescue in the middle of the earth.

L.12: Yet God [is] my King from of old, \q working salvation in the midst of the earth.

R.12: But God has been my King for a very long time. \q He has saved people all over the earth.

decisions.choice: God my King: the turn to trust
decisions.reason: The psalm turns from complaint to the God who has always been King. Verses 13-17 recall his great acts in creation and at the exodus.

decisions.choice: salvation: acts of rescue
decisions.reason: The plural (yeshu'ot) is deliverances, his many saving acts.

records.source: אַתָּ֤ה פוֹרַ֣רְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ֣ יָ֑ם שִׁבַּ֖רְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֥י תַ֝נִּינִ֗ים עַל־הַמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: You divided by your strength [the] sea; you broke [the] heads of sea monsters on the waters.
pieces: By {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tore the sea in two; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crushed the heads of the dragons in the water.

L.13: You divided [the] sea by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.

R.13: You used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power to split the sea apart. \q You smashed the heads of the sea monsters.

decisions.choice: you divided the sea: the exodus, and creation
decisions.reason: The words recall the dividing of the Red Sea (Exodus 14:21) and also God's victory over the chaos waters at creation. Isaiah 51:9-10 joins the two in the same way.

decisions.choice: sea monsters: pictures of chaos
decisions.reason: The tanninim are great creatures of the sea (Genesis 1:21). Here, as in Isaiah 27:1 and 51:9, they stand for the forces of chaos and the enemies God defeats.

decisions.choice: you: a series of "you" lines
decisions.reason: Verses 13-17 begin seven lines with an emphatic "you" ('attah): it is God, and no other, who did these things.

records.source: אַתָּ֣ה רִ֭צַּצְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֣י לִוְיָתָ֑ן תִּתְּנֶ֥נּוּ מַ֝אֲכָ֗ל לְעָ֣ם לְצִיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: You crushed [the] heads of Leviathan; you gave it [as] food to [the] people, to [the] desert-dwellers.
pieces: You shattered the heads of Leviathan \q and gave it as food to the creatures of the desert.

L.14: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave it [as] food to [the] people, to [the] desert-dwellers.

R.14: You crushed the heads of the great monster Leviathan. \q You fed its body to the wild animals of the desert.

decisions.choice: Leviathan: a many-headed sea monster
decisions.reason: Leviathan is a sea monster of the old stories, pictured with many heads. In the Bible it stands for chaos and for powers opposed to God, all under his rule (104:26; Job 41; Isaiah 27:1).

decisions.choice: to the people, to the desert-dwellers: to the creatures of the desert
alternatives: to the people of the desert
to the sharks of the sea
decisions.reason: "People" ('am) can be used of creatures, as of ants in Proverbs 30:25. The monster's body is left as food for desert animals.

records.source: אַתָּ֣ה בָ֭קַעְתָּ מַעְיָ֣ן וָנָ֑חַל אַתָּ֥ה ה֝וֹבַ֗שְׁתָּ נַהֲר֥וֹת אֵיתָֽן׃
records.gloss: You split open spring and torrent; you dried up rivers of constant flow.
pieces: You broke open springs and brooks; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made rivers that always flowed run dry.

L.15: You split open spring and torrent; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} dried up ever-flowing rivers.

R.15: You made water burst out of the ground. \q You made great rivers dry up.

decisions.choice: water from the rock; the Jordan dried up
decisions.reason: God split the rock to give water in the desert (Exodus 17:6; 78:15) and dried up the Jordan for Israel to cross (Joshua 3:13-17).

decisions.choice: ever-flowing: never failing
decisions.reason: The word ('etan) means lasting, a river that flows all year.

records.source: לְךָ֣ י֭וֹם אַף־לְךָ֥ לָ֑יְלָה אַתָּ֥ה הֲ֝כִינ֗וֹתָ מָא֥וֹר וָשָֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: Yours [is the] day, also yours [is the] night; you established [the] light and [the] sun.
pieces: The day is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, and the night is {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} as well; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set the moon and the sun in their places.

L.16: Yours [is the] day, also {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} [is the] night; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} established [the] light and [the] sun.

R.16: Both day and night belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You put the sun and the moon in the sky.

decisions.choice: light: a light in the sky, the moon
decisions.reason: The word (ma'or) is a light-giver, used of the sun and moon in Genesis 1:16. Set beside the sun, it is probably the moon, the light of the night.

decisions.choice: Genesis 1:14-18
decisions.reason: The God who made day and night and the lights to rule them is Lord of all time.

records.source: אַתָּ֣ה הִ֭צַּבְתָּ כָּל־גְּבוּל֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ קַ֥יִץ וָ֝חֹ֗רֶף אַתָּ֥ה יְצַרְתָּם׃
records.gloss: You set all [the] boundaries of [the] earth; summer and winter, you formed them.
pieces: You fixed every boundary of the earth; \q summer and winter are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} handiwork.

L.17: You set all [the] boundaries of [the] earth; \q summer and winter — {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} formed them.

R.17: You set the edges of the earth. \q You made summer and winter.

decisions.choice: the boundaries of the earth: the limits God set
decisions.reason: God set the bounds of land and sea (104:9; Job 38:8-11) and of the nations (Deuteronomy 32:8).

decisions.choice: Genesis 8:22
decisions.reason: God promised that summer and winter would not cease.

records.source: זְכָר־זֹ֗את א֭וֹיֵב חֵרֵ֣ף׀יְהוָ֑ה וְעַ֥ם נָ֝בָ֗ל נִֽאֲצ֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Remember this: [the] enemy has taunted, YHWH, and a foolish people has spurned your name.
pieces: Remember this, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}: the enemy has jeered at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and a foolish people has insulted {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.18: Remember this: [the] enemy has taunted, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and a foolish people has spurned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.18: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember how the enemy has made fun of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q People who have no sense have insulted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: YHWH: God addressed by name
alternatives: the enemy has taunted the LORD
decisions.reason: The name is best taken as an address, "LORD". It may also be the object, "the enemy has taunted the LORD". It is the only use of the name in this psalm, which otherwise says "God".

decisions.choice: foolish: godless
decisions.reason: The fool (naval) is the one who lives as if there were no God (14:1; Deuteronomy 32:21).

decisions.choice: at you
decisions.reason: "Taunted" has no object; the context shows it is God who is mocked.

records.source: אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭חַיַּת נֶ֣פֶשׁ תּוֹרֶ֑ךָ חַיַּ֥ת עֲ֝נִיֶּ֗יךָ אַל־תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃
records.gloss: Do not give to [the] beast [of] desire your turtledove; [the] life of your afflicted do not forget forever.
pieces: Do not let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dove fall prey to the greedy beasts; \q do not leave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} suffering people forgotten for good.

L.19: Do not give the soul of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} turtledove to the wild beast; \q do not forget the life of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} afflicted forever.

R.19: Your people are as weak as a dove. Do not hand them over to the wild animals. \q Do not forget forever those who are suffering.

decisions.choice: your turtledove: God's helpless people
decisions.reason: Israel is pictured as a dove, weak and defenseless, at the mercy of wild animals (Hosea 7:11).

decisions.choice: to the beast the life of your dove
alternatives: to the greedy beast (beast of appetite)
decisions.reason: The words can be read "to the beast, the life of your dove" or "to the beast of appetite, your dove"; either way the dove is to be torn apart.

decisions.choice: Your people are as weak as a dove
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: הַבֵּ֥ט לַבְּרִ֑ית כִּ֥י מָלְא֥וּ מַחֲשַׁכֵּי־אֶ֝֗רֶץ נְא֣וֹת חָמָֽס׃
records.gloss: Look to the covenant, for the dark places of [the] land are full [of the] haunts of violence.
pieces: Pay heed to the covenant, \q because every dark corner of the land is filled with places of violence.

L.20: Look to the covenant, \q for the dark places of [the] land are full [of the] haunts of violence.

R.20: Remember the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made to us. \q All over the land, in its dark places, violent people are waiting.

decisions.choice: the covenant: God's binding promise to his people
decisions.reason: God bound himself to Israel by covenant (Exodus 24:8). The plea is that he keep his own promise.

decisions.choice: the dark places full of haunts of violence: violence everywhere
decisions.reason: The "dark places" may be hiding places where violent men lurk, or the land under the shadow of disaster.

decisions.choice: the promise you made to us
decisions.reason: Readable says what the covenant is (m1).

records.source: אַל־יָשֹׁ֣ב דַּ֣ךְ נִכְלָ֑ם עָנִ֥י וְ֝אֶבְי֗וֹן יְֽהַלְל֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Let not [the] oppressed turn back humiliated; let [the] afflicted and needy praise your name.
pieces: Do not let the downtrodden go back ashamed; \q may the poor and the needy give praise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.21: Let not [the] oppressed turn back humiliated; \q let [the] afflicted and needy praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.21: Do not let people who are mistreated go away ashamed. \q Let poor people and those in need praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the oppressed: the crushed
decisions.reason: The word (dakh) is someone crushed or downtrodden (9:10; 10:18).

decisions.choice: turn back humiliated: leave in shame with the prayer unanswered
decisions.reason: Those who come to God for help are not to go away disappointed.

records.source: קוּמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים רִיבָ֣ה רִיבֶ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר חֶרְפָּתְךָ֥ מִנִּי־נָ֝בָ֗ל כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Arise, God, plead your case; remember your reproach from [the] fool all the day.
pieces: Rise up, God! Take up {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own case; \q keep in mind the insults the fool throws at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all day long.

L.22: Arise, God, plead {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} [own] case; \q remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} reproach from [the] fool all the day.

R.22: Get up, God! Fight for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own cause. \q Do not forget how foolish people insult {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all day.

decisions.choice: Arise: Numbers 10:35
decisions.reason: The cry recalls Moses' words when the ark set out, "Arise, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered" (Numbers 10:35; Psalm 3:8).

decisions.choice: plead your case: defend your own cause
decisions.reason: God is asked to act as his own advocate, for the enemies' insults are against him (verses 10, 18).

decisions.choice: Rise up (B); Get up (R)
decisions.reason: As in the other psalms.

records.source: אַל־תִּ֭שְׁכַּח ק֣וֹל צֹרְרֶ֑יךָ שְׁא֥וֹן קָ֝מֶ֗יךָ עֹלֶ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: Do not forget [the] voice of your foes, [the] uproar of those who rise against you, going up continually.
pieces: Do not ignore the shouting of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies, \q the din of those who rise against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, which never stops rising.

L.23: Do not forget the voice of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foes, \q the uproar of those who rise against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, which goes up continually.

R.23: Do not forget the noise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies make. \q The shouting of those who fight against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gets louder all the time.

decisions.choice: uproar: roar, tumult
decisions.reason: The word (she'on) is used of the roar of the sea and of the nations (65:8). It recalls the enemies' roaring in the temple (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the psalm ends without an answer
decisions.reason: Like Psalm 89, this lament ends with the plea still open: the enemies' noise goes up before God, and the people wait for him to act.
